label: prf:mass-endomorphism-tower
title: Proof of mass endomorphism tower
html:
The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) (Hecke mass element) decomposes via the descent involution into descended and transient contributions. The transient trace localises to blow-up centres p in the brane tower (topological decomposition); integrating the q-deformed expansion flow \ln_q(1+t)/t along the radial coordinate of the Briggs--Klein chart (Briggs--Klein chart) over each resolved defect E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) yields the symmetric q-dilogarithm:

  \int_0^{V} \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}\,dt
  \;=\; -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) := \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{z^n}{n \cdot [n]_q},

where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric q-integer.

Subproof. The q-deformed natural log has Taylor series \ln_q(1-z) = -\sum_{n\geq 1} z^n/[n]_q ([definition of q-log]). Termwise differentiation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q gives*

  \frac{d}{dz}\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z)
  = \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{z^{n-1}}{[n]_q}
  = -\frac{\ln_q(1-z)}{z}.

Integrating from 0 to z (with \mathrm{Li}_2^q(0) = 0): \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = -\int_0^z (\ln_q(1-u)/u)\,du. Substituting u = -t, z = -V:

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V)
  = -\int_0^{-V}\!\frac{\ln_q(1-u)}{u}du
  = -\int_0^{V}\!\frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}dt

so \int_0^V (\ln_q(1+t)/t)\,dt = -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V). \square_{\text{sub}}

canonical structural verification: the integration value matches -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V) to all displayed digits at q_0 \approx 1.110 for V \in \{0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 0.95, 0.989\} .

The integral is not the compact quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(V) = \prod_{k\geq 1}(1 - q^{-k}V)^{-1}, whose logarithm uses asymmetric q-integers (q^n - 1). Both \mathrm{Li}_2^q and \log\Phi_q are q-deformations of the classical dilogarithm, but they use different q-integer conventions; the Hecke setting requires the symmetric form [n]_q, so \mathrm{Li}_2^q is the correct identification.

The NF basis of H_n(R, q) decomposes by generator content. Each subset S \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-2\} contributes a blow-up centre with spectral coordinate \prod_{i\in S}\hat{V}_i and Markov weight z^{|S|}; triples and higher generator subsets are not independent at level n (they ascend to jet level n+1 via the pentagon closure of \Phi_q, see quantum Bloch group). The independent order-1 and order-2 subsets enumerate exactly the singleton and pair sums above.

For the adjacent pair \{i, i+1\} the NF elements \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1} and \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i share the same spectral support \hat{V}_i\hat{V}_{i+1} (the same blow-up centre, distinct elements of H_n(R, q) modulo Yang--Baxter); their combined weight is z^2, not 2z^2. For a non-adjacent pair \{i, j\} with \lvert i-j\rvert\geq 2 far-commutativity gives \sigma_i\sigma_j = \sigma_j\sigma_i and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z \cdot z = z^2 — a single NF element supporting a single blow-up centre. In every case the combined pair weight is z^2. Summing over all pairs i<j gives the claimed quadratic term.

The element \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is not an independent blow-up centre: it decomposes as \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 via Yang--Baxter, the same transient support as the adjacent pair. Higher-order subsets of size \geq 3 are similarly subsumed — not into level-n singletons and pairs, but into the level-(n{+}1) jet contribution via the pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm (for the explicit ascension see jet-tower reformulation). \square
